data: Second Chinese lunar orbiter; first spacecraft flyby of asteroid 4179 Toutatis (Dec 13, 2012, ~770 m closest approach)
Skeleton entry for /fleet (PRD-012 v0.2 / Phase A scaffold). Builder + agency + first-flight per public sources. Specs and gallery TBD in later phases.
Second Chinese lunar orbiter; first to visit asteroid 4179 Toutatis

China's second lunar orbiter, launched 2010-10-01. Chang'e 2 orbited the Moon from 2010 to 2011, then departed lunar orbit in June 2011 for an extended deep-space mission. It proceeded to the Sun-Earth L2 point (arriving August 2011), then departed L2 in April 2012 for a historic flyby of asteroid 4179 Toutatis, executing a close approach on 2012-12-13 at ~770 m distance — the first spacecraft to visit the asteroid. After the Toutatis encounter, Chang'e 2 continued into deep space on a heliocentric trajectory, becoming a drifting interplanetary object.
China's first lunar mission. 200-m global topo map; deliberate Mare Fecunditatis impact 2009-03-01 — first Chinese object on the Moon
First Chinese Mars mission; delivered Zhurong
Japan's first Venus orbiter; recovered from a 2010 orbit-insertion failure to study cloud-top dynamics
NASA's active lunar recon orbiter. LROC's 0.5 m/pixel imagery is the source of every Apollo + Luna + Chang'e landing-site photo here
India's first Moon mission. Discovered widespread surface water on the Moon (M3 + MIP, 2009). Lost contact 2009-08-29 after only 312 days

Began as a higher-resolution remap of the Moon following Chang'e 1, then repurposed for an extended deep-space mission. After completing lunar mapping in 2011, Chang'e 2 departed for Sun-Earth L2 — China's first deep-space mission — and then on to a 2012 flyby of asteroid 4179 Toutatis. Still tracked in heliocentric orbit.
